maya: Heads-up — after running the 8h long-context replay on staging I saw steady memory growth + a small but consistent alignment drift in KV tags when prefetching pages. Repro steps attached.

raj: Can you paste the failing log lines? Also which model/config?

maya: model=redwood/long-prefetch-16k, runtime=main@c3f4a2e. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T22:14:02Z] kv_prefetch: page_id=42, requested_offset=8192, stored_offset=8188
[2026-03-17T22:14:02Z] kv_insert: tag=0x7f3b, slot=1024, token_index=4512
[2026-03-17T22:14:02Z] kv_lookup: got_tag=0x7f39, matched_slot=1023 (mismatch)
```
I reproduced by running the synthetic long-context generator with many small continuation requests (avg len 6). Memory creeps ~0.5% per hour.

lina: Hmm, getting different tag on lookup suggests stale block or off-by-4 bytes in the offset. Is prefetch using the page header size anywhere?

diego: It might be the prefetch path that merges fragments: prefetch reads raw pages and appends into slot buffer using computed append_offset. If append_offset doesn't factor in the header/align_pad we can end up writing a block shifted relative to where lookup expects.

maya: Agreed. I added extra logging around prefetch append_offset and saw sometimes append_offset % 8 == 4 before write, which explains the 2-token misalignment.

raj: Would that cause cross-request contamination too? If a write overlaps previous data but tags don't get rotated/invalidated, you can get stale reads.

maya: Exactly. On rollover (when slot pointer wraps) we sometimes skip explicitly clearing small tail fragments because we assume next write will overwrite. But with misaligned write, the tail remains with old tag bits.

ci-bot: CI failure posted: //ci.redwood/long-contexts:kv-repro flakes on staging-4 (build c3f4a2e). Test: kv_prefetch_alignment_test.

lina: Patch idea: ensure prefetch append computes aligned_offset = round_up(raw_offset + header_size, ALIGNMENT) and always zero-fill the gap between aligned_offset and write_start. Also add a sanity check on lookup: if tag mismatch but token_distance < 8, treat as potential alignment issue and ignore match (to avoid returning stale).

diego: I can prototype a minimal fix. Quick diff: 
```diff
diff --git a/runtime/kv_prefetch.cc b/runtime/kv_prefetch.cc
index 9f8c1a2..d3b7b4f 100644
--- a/runtime/kv_prefetch.cc
+++ b/runtime/kv_prefetch.cc
@@ -120,6 +120,12 @@ void Prefetch::apply(Page &p) {
-  size_t append_offset = p.raw_offset + p.body_len;
+  // account for page header and align to slot granularity to avoid token shift
+  size_t raw_write_start = p.raw_offset + p.body_len;
+  size_t aligned_offset = (raw_write_start + PAGE_HEADER_SIZE + (SLOT_ALIGN-1)) & ~(SLOT_ALIGN-1);
+  size_t append_offset = aligned_offset;
+  // zero-fill gap to prevent stale tag tails
+  memset(slot_buf + orig_append, 0, append_offset - orig_append);
   memcpy(slot_buf + append_offset, p.data, p.data_len);
 }
```

lina: Add unit test that crafts two small fragments where second fragment would previously be misaligned and verify tag mismatch disappears after fix. Also add fuzzing harness for prefetch emit/consume.

maya: Diego — can you open a hotfix branch and include the test? Assign me to validate on staging.

diego: Yep. Creating branch: hotfix/kv-prefetch-align-1949. Will push PR in ~30m.

raj: If this lands, let's also add a perf regression check — alignment fix may add a tiny copy/zero cost. Run the perf test suite and compare tokens/sec for the long-context job. If regress > 1.5% we need to consider optimizing zero-fill (memset could be lazy or use pointer tricks).

maya: Good call. I'll add perf runs to the PR checklist.

ci-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/482 (hotfix/kv-prefetch-align-1949) — CI queued.

lina: Thanks — this smells like the same root cause as the weird leak we saw on staging last month but smaller scale. If this patch stabilizes, we should backport to dedicated runtimes and add a long-context nightly with varied small-frag sizes.

maya: I'll schedule the nightly and attach the new kv_prefetch_alignment_test. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
